newsitem.title: USA: US foreign crude offerings abound, activity light.
newsitem.headline: US foreign crude offerings abound, activity light.

text.p: Offers for North Sea Brent and other foreign crudes remained plentiful on Friday although dealings were light amid an industry-sponsored golf tournament in Houston, traders said.
Brent was on offer at 70 cents discount to West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for delivery around late-June, traders said.
The asking price climbed some seven cents from Thursday, reflecting the narrowing WTI/Brent spread and the rising dated Brent price.
June WTI/Brent was around $1.55-65 a barrel Friday afternoon.
Across the Atlantic, a wet Brent cargo loading May 18-20 was sold at June Brent minus 20 cents a barrel, up five cents from Thursday.
A trading house was heard to have sold a Brent to a Gulf Coast refiner on Thursday for June 10-15 at WTI minus 80 cents a barrel.
One of two Oseberg cargoes for mid-May arrival was sold on Friday, at an unconfirmed price of around WTI minus 80 cents a barrel, traders said.
Among West African grades, a U.S. refiner sold a prompt Rabi cargo to another refiner on the Gulf Coast at WTI minus $1.03 a barrel into the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP).
In Latin America, activity was muted with the exception of a closely watched tender for two Cusiana tenders issued by Colombian state Ecopetrol.
The cargoes load June 3-7 and June 5-9.
The awards are expected imminently, traders said.
